content.title: About
content.content: Grated Parmesan is a hard cheese made from cow's milk, produced in the Italian regions of Parma and surrounding areas. It has a sharp, nutty, slightly sweet flavor and a characteristic granular texture. Parmesan is commonly used as a topping for pasta, risotto, salads, and baked dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The term “Parmesan” is protected by a PDO (Protected Designation of Origin) and can only be used for cheese produced in specific Italian regions.
Traditional Parmesan is aged from 12 to 36 months; the longer the aging, the more intense the flavor.
It is often called the “king of cheeses” because of its versatility and rich taste.
The gritty texture comes from tyrosine crystals that form during long aging.
In Italy, Parmesan is frequently served as thin shavings rather than a fine powder.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Parmesan provides about 1,100 mg of calcium per 100 g, supporting bone and dental health.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: It contains roughly 35 g of complete protein per 100 g, essential for tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The cheese is a good source of vitamin B12, riboflavin (B2) and niacin (B3), which aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Low in lactose
items.content: Extended aging breaks down most lactose, making Parmesan generally well‑tolerated by those with mild lactose intolerance.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Vitamin A and selenium content help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Milk‑protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to casein or whey may react to Parmesan.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Grated Parmesan contains about 1,800 mg of sodium per 100 g, which can be a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: It provides roughly 430 kcal per 100 g, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: Those prone to gout should monitor intake, as cheese contains purines that can raise uric acid levels.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sprinkle grated Parmesan over pasta, risotto, soups, salads, and casseroles. It can be added directly before serving or used as a flavor base by sautéing in butter. For a milder taste, use freshly grated cheese.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep grated Parmesan in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0–4 °C. It stays fresh for 2–3 weeks. For longer storage, freeze in small portions to preserve aroma.
